s883.content:
Botolph was an English abbot who founded a monastery in 654 at a place called Icanho in East Anglia, and taught there until his death around 680. Abbots came from far away to learn from him.

He became one of the best-loved saints of England. Churches dedicated to him were often built by the gates of towns, where travelers set out and arrived, and Boston in Lincolnshire, “Botolph’s town,” bears his name.
s883.intercession: St. Botolph, pray for us, and for all who travel. Amen.

s884.content:
Guthlac was a young Mercian noble who led a war band for nine years, until, thinking of the deaths of the great men of old, he turned to God and became a monk at Repton. Two years later he went into the fens and settled as a hermit on the island of Crowland, in a hollow of an old burial mound.

There he lived in prayer and fasting, struggling with demons and receiving those who came for counsel, among them the exiled prince Æthelbald, whose kingship he foretold. He died in 714, and Crowland Abbey was later built over his cell.
s884.intercession: St. Guthlac, pray for us, that we may turn from war to peace. Amen.

s885.content:
Comgall was the founder and first abbot of Bangor, on the shores of Belfast Lough in Ireland, around 555. It became one of the great monasteries of Europe, where thousands of monks lived under his strict rule, and its prayer was sung day and night.

From Bangor St. Columbanus and St. Gall set out to bring the Gospel to the Continent. Comgall was a friend of St. Columba, and traveled with him to the king of the Picts.
s885.intercession: St. Comgall, pray for us, and for the Church in Ireland. Amen.

s886.content:
Finnian was an Irish monk who studied at Candida Casa, St. Ninian’s monastery in Scotland, and in Rome, and founded the abbey of Movilla in County Down around 540. He was a teacher of St. Columba.

He brought back a precious book of the Scriptures; tradition says that when Columba secretly copied it, Finnian claimed the copy, and the king judged that “to every cow her calf, to every book its copy,” a quarrel that ended in a battle and in Columba’s exile to Iona.
s886.intercession: St. Finnian, pray for us, and for all who love and copy books. Amen.

s887.content:
Enda was a warrior prince of Oriel in Ulster who was converted by his sister, St. Fanchea, an abbess, and became a monk. Around 484 he founded a monastery at Killeany on Inishmore, the largest of the Aran Islands, in the Atlantic off the coast of Galway.

He is called the patriarch of Irish monasticism: many of the great saints of Ireland, among them St. Ciarán of Clonmacnoise and St. Brendan, are said to have come to Aran to learn from him.
s887.intercession: St. Enda, pray for us, and for all who seek God at the edges of the world. Amen.

s888.content:
Fursey was an Irish monk who, during a grave illness, had visions of the life after death, of angels and demons and the fires of the world to come, which were written down and read across Europe; St. Bede tells of them.

Around 630 he crossed to East Anglia, where King Sigeberht gave him an old Roman fort to found a monastery, and from there he preached the Gospel. Later he went to France, founded a monastery at Lagny, and died there in 650.
s888.intercession: St. Fursey, pray for us, that we may live in the light of eternity. Amen.

s889.content:
Adomnán was the ninth abbot of Iona, the monastery founded by St. Columba, and wrote his Life of Columba, the most important work of its kind from early Scotland.

At the Synod of Birr in 697 he persuaded the kings and churchmen of Ireland and Scotland to accept the Law of the Innocents, which protected women, children, and clergy from violence in war, with penalties for those who harmed them. It is one of the first laws in Europe to protect the innocent in war.
s889.intercession: St. Adomnán, pray for us, and for all who suffer in war. Amen.

s890.content:
Mochuda, also called Carthage, was abbot of Rahan in the Irish midlands, where he ruled hundreds of monks. Around 636 he and his community were driven out by a local king, and they walked south together across Ireland.

At Lismore, by the river Blackwater, he founded a new monastery, which became a great school drawing students from Ireland and abroad. He died there in 637.
s890.intercession: St. Mochuda, pray for us, and for all who are driven from their homes. Amen.

s891.content:
Pirmin was a wandering monk, perhaps from Spain or Gaul, who came to the Alemanni of southwestern Germany and founded or restored many monasteries there. The greatest was the abbey on the island of Reichenau in Lake Constance, founded in 724.

He wrote a short handbook of the faith for new Christians, the Scarapsus, one of the oldest texts to give the Apostles’ Creed in the form we say today.
s891.intercession: St. Pirmin, pray for us, and for all who teach the faith. Amen.

s892.content:
Bernardo was a noble and a lawyer of Siena who, at about forty, left the city with two friends to live as hermits on his family’s land at Accona. Others joined them, and they built the monastery of Monte Oliveto Maggiore, following the Rule of St. Benedict, in honor of the Virgin Mary.

He was the abbot of the new congregation, the Olivetans, for many years. When the Black Death came in 1348 he went into Siena with his monks to care for the sick, and died there of the plague with many of them. He was canonized in 2009.
s892.intercession: St. Bernardo, pray for us, and for all who care for the sick in time of plague. Amen.

s893.content:
Peter is honored as the first hermit of Mount Athos, the Holy Mountain of Greece. As the story is told, he was a soldier taken captive by the Arabs, who prayed to St. Nicholas and St. Simeon and was set free.

Going on to Rome, he became a monk, and then, by a sign from the Mother of God, he went to Athos, where he lived alone in a cave for some fifty years. He was found there, near the end of his life, by a hunter. Thousands of monks have followed him to the Holy Mountain.
s893.intercession: St. Peter, pray for us, and for all the monks of the Holy Mountain. Amen.

s894.content:
Luke, called “the Younger” and the wonderworker, was a hermit of central Greece who lived in prayer on the slopes of Mount Helicon and was known for his gifts of healing and prophecy. He is said to have foretold that the island of Crete would be taken back from the Arabs, as it was some years after his death.

Over his tomb grew the monastery of Hosios Loukas, “the holy Luke,” whose church, with its golden mosaics, is one of the masterpieces of Byzantine art.
s894.intercession: St. Luke, pray for us, that our lives may be full of God’s light. Amen.

s895.content:
Æbbe was a princess of Northumbria, the sister of the kings St. Oswald and Oswiu. She became a nun and founded a double monastery of men and women at Coldingham, on the coast of what is now southern Scotland, at the headland still called St. Abb’s Head.

St. Cuthbert came to visit her there. St. Bede tells that the monastery grew lax in her old age, and that after her death it burned; but she herself was remembered as a holy and wise mother.
s895.intercession: St. Æbbe, pray for us, and for all who lead communities. Amen.

s896.content:
Pierre-Joseph Cassant was a boy of southwestern France with a poor memory, who failed at his studies and was turned away when he hoped to be a priest. At sixteen he entered the Trappist monastery of Sainte-Marie-du-Désert, where a kind novice master saw his goodness and helped him.

Taking the name Marie-Joseph, he struggled patiently through his studies and was ordained a priest in 1902. A few months later he fell ill with tuberculosis, and he died in 1903, at twenty-five, having offered his sufferings for priests. He was beatified in 2004, a patron of all who find learning hard.
s896.intercession: Bl. Marie-Joseph, pray for us, and for all who struggle to learn. Amen.

s897.content:
Maria Sagheddu was a stubborn, quick-tempered girl from Sardinia who changed after the death of her sister and gave herself to God. At twenty-one she entered the Trappistine monastery at Grottaferrata, near Rome, taking the name Maria Gabriella.

When her abbess spoke to the community about the week of prayer for Christian unity in 1938, Maria Gabriella offered her life for the unity of Christians. Soon after she fell ill with tuberculosis, and she died on Good Shepherd Sunday in 1939, at twenty-five. Pope John Paul II beatified her in 1983.
s897.intercession: Bl. Maria Gabriella, pray for us, that all may be one. Amen.

s898.content:
Angelo Ercole Menni was a young bank clerk of Milan who, moved by the wounded soldiers he helped carry from the battlefield, joined the Brothers Hospitallers of St. John of God, taking the name Benedict. At twenty-six he was sent to Spain, where the order had been suppressed, and in the face of revolution and danger he restored it, founding hospitals across Spain, Portugal, and Latin America.

He gave his life especially to the mentally ill, whom many neglected, and in 1881 founded the Sisters Hospitallers of the Sacred Heart of Jesus to care for women with mental illness. He died in France in 1914 and was canonized in 1999.
s898.intercession: St. Benedict, pray for us, and for all who suffer from mental illness. Amen.

s899.content:
Christian de Chergé was the prior of the Trappist monastery of Our Lady of Atlas at Tibhirine, in the mountains of Algeria, where a small community of French monks lived in friendship with their Muslim neighbors. During the civil war of the 1990s, they chose to stay, knowing the danger.

In March 1996 seven of the monks were kidnapped by armed Islamists, and in May they were killed. Christian had left a testament forgiving in advance whoever would kill him, whom he called “my friend of the last minute,” hoping to see him in heaven. The seven monks were beatified in 2018 with twelve other martyrs of Algeria.
s899.intercession: Bl. Christian and companions, pray for us, and for peace between Christians and Muslims. Amen.

s900.content:
Pierre Claverie was born in Algiers and grew up in the French community there, which he later said lived as if behind a bubble, without truly knowing its Muslim neighbors. As a Dominican friar he learned Arabic, studied Islam, and gave his life to friendship and dialogue, and in 1981 he became bishop of Oran.

He stayed with his people through the civil war, though his life was threatened. On August 1, 1996, he was killed by a bomb at the door of his house, together with his young Muslim friend and driver, Mohamed Bouchikhi, their blood mingled together. He was beatified with the martyrs of Algeria in 2018.
s900.intercession: Bl. Pierre, pray for us, that we may build friendship where there is fear. Amen.

s901.content:
Robert was a priest of Yorkshire who joined the monks who left St. Mary’s Abbey in York in 1132 to live more strictly, and so became one of the founders of Fountains Abbey, which joined the Cistercians.

In 1138 he was sent to found a new abbey at Newminster, near Morpeth in Northumberland, and he was its abbot until his death. He was a friend of St. Godric of Finchale, who is said to have seen his soul carried to heaven.
s901.intercession: St. Robert, pray for us, that we may follow Christ more closely. Amen.

s902.content:
Wandrille was a count at the court of the Frankish king Dagobert who, with his wife’s agreement, left the world, and both entered religious life. He lived as a monk in several places, including St. Columbanus’s monastery at Bobbio, before being ordained by St. Ouen of Rouen.

In 649 he founded the abbey of Fontenelle in Normandy, which grew to hundreds of monks and became a great center of learning. The abbey, now called Saint-Wandrille, still has monks today.
s902.intercession: St. Wandrille, pray for us, that we may leave all to follow Christ. Amen.

s903.content:
Philibert grew up at the court of King Dagobert and became a monk at twenty. In 654 he founded the abbey of Jumièges in Normandy, on land given by Queen Bathilde, and it became one of the great abbeys of France.

He spoke out against the injustice of the powerful mayor of the palace, Ebroin, and was driven from his abbey and imprisoned for a time. He went on to found the monastery of Noirmoutier on an island off the Atlantic coast, where he died.
s903.intercession: St. Philibert, pray for us, that we may speak the truth to the powerful. Amen.

s904.content:
Columba was born at Rieti in Italy and, refusing the marriage her parents had arranged, became a Dominican tertiary at nineteen, cutting off her hair and dedicating herself to Christ. She lived a life of severe fasting and prayer and received visions and ecstasies.

She went to Perugia, where she founded a convent of Dominican sisters, and the people came to love her for her counsel and her charity in times of war and plague. She was beatified in 1625 and is a patron of the city.
s904.intercession: Bl. Columba, pray for us, and for the cities where we live. Amen.

s905.content:
Bertin was a monk of Luxeuil, the great monastery of St. Columbanus, who went with two companions to help St. Omer bring the Gospel to the region of the Morini in northern France.

On land given by Omer he founded the abbey of Sithiu, later called Saint-Bertin, and governed it for many decades. So many came to him that more than 150 monks lived under his rule, and the town of Saint-Omer grew up around the abbey and the church.
s905.intercession: St. Bertin, pray for us, and for all who work together for the Gospel. Amen.

s906.content:
Omer was a monk of Luxeuil who, around 637, was made bishop of Thérouanne, among the Morini of northern France, where the faith had almost died out. He preached tirelessly, and with St. Bertin and his companions he founded monasteries to plant the Gospel in the region.

In old age he went blind, but went on visiting and teaching his people. The town of Saint-Omer bears his name.
s906.intercession: St. Omer, pray for us, and for all who rebuild the faith in their land. Amen.

s907.content:
Lanfranc was a lawyer of Pavia who became a monk at the poor new abbey of Bec in Normandy, and made its school famous across Europe; St. Anselm came there to study under him. He defended the Church’s faith in the real presence of Christ in the Eucharist against the teaching of Berengar of Tours.

In 1070 he was made archbishop of Canterbury, and he rebuilt the cathedral and reformed the Church in England after the Norman Conquest. He died in 1089, and Anselm succeeded him.
s907.intercession: Bl. Lanfranc, pray for us, that we may believe and adore the Body of Christ. Amen.

s908.content:
Gilbert was a parish priest of Sempringham in Lincolnshire who gathered seven young women to live a life of prayer, then added lay sisters and lay brothers to serve them, and canons to be their priests. The Cistercians declined to take them in, and so he founded the Gilbertine Order, the only religious order founded in medieval England.

By his death it had thirteen houses. He lived simply all his life, and died at more than a hundred years old. He was canonized in 1202.
s908.intercession: St. Gilbert, pray for us, and for all who serve the Church in their parish. Amen.

s909.content:
William was a monk of Regensburg, a scholar of music and astronomy, who in 1069 became abbot of Hirsau in the Black Forest. He brought there the customs of Cluny, and from Hirsau the reform spread to more than a hundred monasteries in Germany.

He took the side of the pope in the struggle with the emperor over the appointment of bishops, and gave lay brothers an important place in monastic life. He died in 1091.
s909.intercession: Bl. William, pray for us, and for the renewal of the Church. Amen.

s910.content:
Otto was a priest at the court of the emperor who became bishop of Bamberg in 1102. He was a builder of churches and monasteries, founding or restoring more than twenty.

At the request of the duke of Poland he went twice, in 1124 and 1128, as a missionary to Pomerania, on the Baltic coast, and baptized thousands there with patience and gentleness, refusing to use force. He is called the apostle of Pomerania, and was canonized in 1189.
s910.intercession: St. Otto, pray for us, that we may spread the Gospel with patience. Amen.

s911.content:
Godric was a poor boy of Norfolk who became a peddler, then a sea merchant and ship’s captain, sailing the seas of northern Europe. A visit to the holy island of Lindisfarne turned his heart, and he made pilgrimages to Rome and to Jerusalem.

He then lived for sixty years as a hermit at Finchale, near Durham, by the river Wear, in prayer and penance, and was known for his gentleness to animals. Some of the oldest songs in the English language, hymns to the Virgin Mary, are his.
s911.intercession: St. Godric, pray for us, and for all who work at sea. Amen.

s912.content:
Stephen was a priest of the Limousin, in central France, who with a companion left everything to live as a hermit in the forest. Others came, and he founded the monastery of Obazine, and a monastery of women nearby, where his own mother became a nun.

In 1147 his communities joined the Cistercian Order. He was known for his love of poverty and of the poor.
s912.intercession: St. Stephen, pray for us, that we may love poverty and the poor. Amen.

s913.content:
Albino Luciani was the son of a poor working family in the Dolomites of northern Italy. As a priest, a teacher in the seminary, and then bishop of Vittorio Veneto and patriarch of Venice, he was known for his simplicity, his humor, and his gift of explaining the faith so that anyone could understand it; he once wrote a book of letters to famous people, from Pinocchio to Charles Dickens.

Elected pope in August 1978, he chose the names of his two predecessors and refused the papal coronation. He smiled so often that he was called “the smiling pope.” He died suddenly after only thirty-three days. Pope Francis beatified him in 2022.
s913.intercession: Bl. John Paul, pray for us, that we may be humble and joyful. Amen.

s914.content:
Fulton Sheen was a priest of Illinois, a philosopher who taught at the Catholic University of America, and the most famous preacher of his age. His radio program, The Catholic Hour, and then his television series Life Is Worth Living, in the 1950s, reached tens of millions of people, who watched him explain the faith with a blackboard and a smile.

He was national director of the Society for the Propagation of the Faith, raising great sums for the missions, and bishop of Rochester. All his life he kept a daily holy hour before the Blessed Sacrament. He was beatified in 2026.
s914.intercession: Bl. Fulton, pray for us, that we may spend an hour with the Lord each day. Amen.

s915.content:
Dorothy Day was a journalist and radical of New York who, after a restless youth and the birth of her daughter, became a Catholic in 1927. In 1933, with the French thinker Peter Maurin, she founded the Catholic Worker, a newspaper sold for a penny a copy, and houses of hospitality where the poor and homeless were fed and sheltered in the name of Christ.

She lived among the poor for the rest of her life, prayed the psalms every day, and went to prison more than once for her protests against war and injustice. “Don’t call me a saint,” she said; “I don’t want to be dismissed so easily.” Her cause for canonization is open.
s915.intercession: Dorothy Day, pray for us, that we may see Christ in the poor. Amen.

s916.content:
Matt Talbot was a Dublin laborer who began drinking heavily at twelve. At twenty-eight, penniless and ashamed, he took a pledge before a priest to stop drinking for three months, and then for life, and he kept it, with great struggle, through daily Mass and prayer.

For the next forty years he worked on the docks and in a timber yard, went to Mass before work, read and prayed through the night, and gave most of his wages to the poor and the missions. He died on his way to Mass in 1925. He is the patron of all who struggle with addiction.
s916.intercession: Ven. Matt Talbot, pray for all who struggle with addiction. Amen.

s917.content:
Augustus Tolton was born into slavery in Missouri. When he was a boy his mother escaped with her children across the Mississippi to freedom in Illinois. He felt called to the priesthood, but every seminary in the United States refused him because he was Black, and he was trained in Rome.

Ordained in 1886, he became the first recognized Black Catholic priest in the United States. He served in Quincy and then in Chicago, where he built a church for Black Catholics, often facing prejudice from within the Church itself. He died of heatstroke at forty-three. He was declared Venerable in 2019.
s917.intercession: Ven. Augustus Tolton, pray for us, and for an end to racism. Amen.

s918.content:
Bertha Bowman grew up in Mississippi, became a Catholic at nine, and joined the Franciscan Sisters of Perpetual Adoration, the only Black sister in her community, taking the name Thea. She was a teacher and scholar who brought the songs, prayer, and culture of Black Catholics into the life of the Church.

When she was dying of cancer, she spoke to the bishops of the United States from her wheelchair in 1989, and had them stand, cross arms, and sing “We Shall Overcome.” She asked, “What does it mean to be Black and Catholic?” and answered with joy. Her cause for canonization is open.
s918.intercession: Thea Bowman, pray for us, that we may bring our whole selves to God. Amen.

s919.content:
Henriette DeLille was a free woman of color of New Orleans, raised to take a place in a society of arranged unions with white men. Instead she gave her life to God and to the care of the poor, the sick, and the enslaved, whom she taught the faith at a time when it was forbidden to teach them to read.

In 1842 she founded the Sisters of the Holy Family, one of the first congregations of Black sisters in the United States, which still serves today. Her cause for canonization was the first of an African American woman to be opened.
s919.intercession: Henriette DeLille, pray for us, and for all who are scorned for their race. Amen.

s920.content:
Emil Kapaun was the son of Czech farmers in Kansas who became a priest and an Army chaplain. In the Korean War, when his unit was overrun in 1950, he refused to leave the wounded, and was captured with them.

In the prison camp he stole food for the starving men, washed the sick, picked lice from them, said prayers, and kept up their hope, even as he himself fell ill. He died in the camp in 1951. He received the Medal of Honor in 2013, and was declared Venerable in 2025.
s920.intercession: Ven. Emil Kapaun, pray for all soldiers and prisoners of war. Amen.

s921.content:
Vincent Capodanno was a Maryknoll missionary priest from New York who served in Taiwan and Hong Kong before asking to become a chaplain to the Marines in Vietnam. He lived with his men in the field and was called “the grunt padre.”

On September 4, 1967, when his company was ambushed, he went among the wounded under fire, anointing the dying and tending the injured, even after he himself had been wounded several times, until he was killed trying to reach a wounded corpsman. He received the Medal of Honor, and his cause for canonization is open.
s921.intercession: Vincent Capodanno, pray for all who serve in harm’s way. Amen.

s922.content:
Patrick Peyton grew up in a poor family in County Mayo, Ireland, who prayed the Rosary together every evening, and came to America as a young man. As a seminarian he fell gravely ill with tuberculosis and was healed after asking the prayers of Our Lady, and he promised to spend his life making her known.

As a priest of the Congregation of Holy Cross he founded the Family Rosary Crusade, holding great rallies around the world and using radio, film, and television with the help of Hollywood stars. He taught millions that “the family that prays together stays together.”
s922.intercession: Ven. Patrick Peyton, pray for our families, that we may pray together. Amen.
